title: Clinical Photography in UK Podiatric Practice A Narrative Review of Consent, Confidentiality and Safe Image Handling
content: A clinical photograph can show changes that are difficult to describe in words. In podiatry, images help document wounds and skin lesions, support referrals and compare progress over time. They also create a lasting record that may identify the patient, even when the face is absent. This narrative review brings together UK legislation, professional guidance and selected literature to explain how photographs should be taken, stored and used. The starting point is the intended purpose. Agreement to a photograph for care does not automatically permit teaching, research, publication or promotion, and the patient’s agreement is distinct from the organisation’s data-protection basis for processing the image. The proposed framework covers the patient discussion, image capture, record linkage, storage, secondary use and audit. Its practical message is simple: a clinical photograph needs the same care as the rest of the patient’s health record.
